package_info.package_versions: All versions of private packages on npm
package_info.why_malicious: The attack exploits a timing side-channel vulnerability in the npm registry API, allowing attackers to enumerate the existence of private package names. This enables the creation of malicious clones or typosquatted packages, increasing the risk of supply chain attacks by tricking developers into installing compromised packages.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (external enumeration attack initiated by attacker)
execution_context.file_location: External script or tool making HTTP requests to the npm registry API (not within a package itself)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Sends an HTTP GET request to the npm registry for a specific package name, targeting both public and private namespaces, to observe the response time of a 404 error. The attacker repeats this process for multiple package names to collect timing data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is used to systematically probe the npm registry for the existence of private packages by exploiting subtle timing differences in 404 responses, which is not a standard or legitimate use of the API.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package existence checks do not rely on timing analysis of 404 responses; all 404s should be indistinguishable regardless of whether the package is private or non-existent. This code intentionally leverages timing discrepancies to infer sensitive information.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may check for the existence of public packages (e.g., to avoid name collisions), but do not perform repeated timing measurements or attempt to enumerate private package names.
key_indicators: Automated, high-frequency HTTP GET requests to the npm registry for a wide range of package names, especially under private or organizational scopes
Collection and logging of response times for each 404 error received
Targeting of package names that are likely to be private or sensitive

execution_context.trigger: runtime (external enumeration attack, post-request analysis phase)
execution_context.file_location: External script or tool performing timing analysis after receiving HTTP responses

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: if (response_time > threshold) { package_is_private = true; } else { package_is_nonexistent = true; }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Implements logic to compare the response time of the npm registry's 404 error to a predefined threshold. If the response time exceeds the threshold, the script infers that the package exists as a private package; otherwise, it is considered non-existent. This enables automated enumeration of private package names.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This logic is specifically crafted to exploit a timing side-channel, using response time as a covert signal to distinguish between private and non-existent packages, which constitutes an information disclosure attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard package management tools do not analyze HTTP response times to infer the existence of private resources. This approach violates the expectation that private package names remain confidential and indistinguishable from non-existent ones.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Performance monitoring tools may measure response times for network requests, but not for the purpose of inferring the existence of private or restricted resources.
key_indicators: Conditional logic that classifies package existence based on measured HTTP response times for 404 errors
Use of empirically determined thresholds to separate private from non-existent package responses
Automated enumeration and logging of package names classified as private

attack_chain.action: Attacker initiates repeated, automated HTTP GET requests to the npm registry for a list of target package names, including those likely to be private or sensitive.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of response times for each queried package name, building a dataset for timing analysis.

attack_chain.action: Attacker analyzes the collected response times using timing analysis logic to distinguish between private and non-existent packages.
attack_chain.leads_to: Enumeration of private package names belonging to the target organization or scope, revealing confidential information.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates public clones or typosquatted packages with the same or similar names as the discovered private packages, publishing them to the npm registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential supply chain compromise if developers mistakenly install the malicious clones, leading to code execution or data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Automated, repeated HTTP GET requests to the npm registry for package names under a specific organization or scope, especially those not known to be public
Analysis and logging of HTTP 404 response times to infer resource existence
Enumeration patterns targeting a large number of package names in a short time frame
file_indicators: External scripts or tools that systematically enumerate package names and record response times (e.g., scripts containing logic for timing analysis of HTTP 404 responses)
Log files or artifacts showing bursts of 404 requests for non-existent or private package names, especially with associated timing data
network_indicators: High volume of HTTP GET requests to https://registry.npmjs.org/ with varying package names, particularly under private or organizational scopes
Patterns of requests that include both known public and likely private package namespaces, often in rapid succession
Unusual enumeration activity from single IPs or user agents targeting a wide range of package names
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for automated or scripted access patterns to the npm registry that involve repeated 404 responses for package names under your organization's scope, especially when accompanied by timing analysis or logging of response times. Set up alerts for bursts of 404 errors targeting private or sensitive namespaces, and investigate external tools or scripts that perform timing-based enumeration. Correlate network logs with file artifacts to identify enumeration attempts and potential information disclosure.
